name: Quantum BTZ Black Hole
description: The black hole of three dimensions with the backreaction of strongly coupled quantum fields included exactly, read off a black hole on a brane in anti-de Sitter space of four dimensions. One more term in the metric of Bañados, Teitelboim, and Zanelli, $-\ell F/r$, puts a curvature singularity at its centre and hides the conical singularities of negative mass behind horizons.
tags: quantum field theory in curved spacetime
convention: We keep factors of $c$ explicit. The length $\ell_3$ is the anti-de Sitter radius of the brane, and $\ell$ sets the strength of the backreaction.
history: The black hole of Máximo Bañados, Claudio Teitelboim, and Jorge Zanelli, the BTZ black hole, is curved by the same amount at every point, since it is anti-de Sitter space of three dimensions with its points identified [banados1992, banados1993]. Quantum fields outside it still carry energy, and by Einstein's equations that energy should bend the geometry in turn [emparan2020qbtz]. Solving for the metric and the state of the fields together, from $G_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi G\langle T_{\mu\nu}\rangle$, is "often intractable", so the usual approach takes the backreaction to be small and works one order at a time [emparan2020qbtz]. In three dimensions the problem can be solved exactly with holography, which trades strongly coupled quantum fields for classical gravity in four [emparan2020qbtz].¶Late in 1999, Roberto Emparan, Gary T. Horowitz, and Robert C. Myers built exact black holes bound to a brane, a wall with two dimensions of space inside anti-de Sitter space of four [emparan2000branes]. They took the metric of a black hole accelerating in anti-de Sitter space, the C-metric, cut it along a surface, and glued it to a copy of itself, so that the hole sits on the seam [emparan2000branes2, emparan2020qbtz]. Large holes on a flat brane appear as flattened pancakes, "with a relatively small extent off the brane" [emparan2000branes]. On a brane with a negative cosmological constant the largest are "precisely BTZ black holes on the brane", and in the fourth dimension they stretch out as black strings [emparan2000branes2]. The smaller ones stay close to the brane, and for one of them "the horizon looks more like a cigar than a pancake" [emparan2000branes2].¶Emparan, Alessandro Fabbri, and Nemanja Kaloper read the same holes again in 2002, as quantum black holes of three dimensions [emparan2002holograms]. Classical gravity in anti-de Sitter space is dual to a strongly coupled conformal field theory on its boundary, and a brane near that boundary carries the field theory together with gravity [emparan2002holograms]. A black hole on the brane that solves the classical equations in four dimensions is then the dual of a "quantum-corrected" black hole in three, with every planar diagram of the fields included [emparan2002holograms]. On a brane curved like anti-de Sitter space its metric is that of Bañados, Teitelboim, and Zanelli with one more term, which falls off as $1/r$ [emparan2002holograms]. For negative masses, where the classical metric has a naked conical singularity, they found "classical conical spacetimes dressed with a horizon from the backreaction of the Casimir energy" of the fields [emparan2002holograms]. No hole that stays near the brane is heavier than $m = c^2/(24\mathcal{G}_3)$, which is $M = 1/3$, and above that the brane carries the classical metric "without any corrections" [emparan2002holograms, emparan2020qbtz].¶That analysis "was incomplete", and in 2020 Emparan, Antonia Micol Frassino, and Benson Way took the solution up again, rotation and all, and named it quBTZ [emparan2020qbtz]. The quantum correction is one term in the metric, $-\ell F/r$, where the length $\ell$ grows with the number of quantum fields and $F$ is fixed by the mass [emparan2020qbtz]. With it the curvature varies from point to point and diverges at $r = 0$, where the Kretschmann scalar $12/\ell_3^4 + 6\ell^2F^2/r^6$ grows without bound [emparan2020qbtz]. Gravity on the brane also picks up terms in the square of the curvature, which are those of new massive gravity [emparan2020qbtz]. For every mass between $M = 0$ and $M = 1/3$ there are two quantum holes, and both have "higher temperature than the classical one with the same mass" [emparan2020qbtz]. The rotating hole has a ring singularity at $r = 0$, "which was not present in the classical rotating BTZ geometry" [emparan2020qbtz].¶Which entropy obeys the first law of thermodynamics for such a hole? With quantum fields outside, the entropy of a black hole is a quarter of the area of its horizon plus the entanglement entropy of the fields across it, the generalised entropy $S_{\rm gen}$ [emparan2020qbtz]. In four dimensions $S_{\rm gen}$ is the area of the bulk horizon over $4G_4$, the formula of Shinsei Ryu and Tadashi Takayanagi for entanglement entropy applied to a braneworld [emparan2020qbtz, ryu2006]. With the mass and the angular momentum measured on the brane, it obeys the first law "exactly, even in the presence of backreaction and with higher-curvature corrections" [emparan2020qbtz]. The Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of the horizon on the brane does not [emparan2020qbtz]. The entropy lives in the bulk and the mass on the brane, quantities that "belong in different worlds", and their agreement is a test of the whole holographic reading [emparan2020qbtz].¶Quantum fields can stay regular on the inner horizon of the rotating BTZ hole at leading order, which seemed to break strong cosmic censorship [emparan2020scc]. Working in the four dimensional picture, Emparan and Marija Tomašević tied the inner horizon of the hole on the brane to that of a rotating hole in the bulk, and argued that the next order of backreaction makes it singular [emparan2020scc]. Marc Casals, Fabbri, Cristián Martínez, and Zanelli solved the semiclassical equations for a single conformally coupled scalar field to first order, and around the naked singularity of the rotating BTZ metric at negative mass its quantum effects form "a horizon that shields it" [casals2017]. In de Sitter space of three dimensions "classical black holes do not exist", and Emparan, Juan F. Pedraza, Andrew Svesko, Tomašević, and Manus R. Visser built quantum ones there from the same braneworld [emparan2022ds3]. The largest of them is as big as the cosmological horizon, in a limit like Nariai's [emparan2022ds3].

related.text: The classical hole. At $\ell = 0$ the quantum term drops out, and the static chart is the metric of Bañados, Teitelboim, and Zanelli with no rotation [emparan2020qbtz].

The accelerating black hole, here taken in anti-de Sitter space of four dimensions. The quantum BTZ black hole is the metric induced on its surface $x = 0$, where the brane sits [emparan2000branes2, emparan2020qbtz].

Gravity bound to a brane in anti-de Sitter space. Here the brane has two dimensions of space and is curved like anti-de Sitter space itself, the setting of Andreas Karch and Lisa Randall, in which the graviton on the brane has a small mass [karch2001, emparan2020qbtz].

A point particle of three dimensions is a cone. With a negative cosmological constant and quantum fields around it, a cone of negative mass is dressed with a horizon [emparan2002holograms, emparan2020qbtz].
At $M = -1$, where $F = 0$, the static chart is anti-de Sitter space of three dimensions, the lightest state of the brane [emparan2002holograms, emparan2020qbtz].
The BTZ black hole with a shell of null particles on its horizon, the field of a few quanta thrown in from one side long ago [shenker2014].

coordinates.name: Static

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius of the brane, a length; far from the hole the curvature is that of anti-de Sitter space with $\Lambda = -1/\ell_3^2$

Mass, dimensionless, $M = 8\mathcal{G}_3 m/c^2$ for a hole of mass $m$, with $\mathcal{G}_3$ the renormalised Newton's constant in three dimensions; the family covers $-1 \le M \le 1/3$, with $M = 4k/(3 + k)^2$ for a number $k > -1$

Strength of the backreaction of the quantum fields, a length, $\ell \simeq 2c_{\rm CFT}\hbar\mathcal{G}_3/c^3$ for small $\ell/\ell_3$ and a conformal field theory of central charge $c_{\rm CFT}$; at $\ell = 0$ the hole is the classical one of Bañados, Teitelboim, and Zanelli
Strength of the stress tensor of the quantum fields, dimensionless and fixed by the mass: $F = 8(1 + k)/(3 + k)^3$, where $M = 4k/(3 + k)^2$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $\phi$ of period $2\pi$, and write $H = r^2/\ell_3^2 - M - \ell F/r$, whose positive root is the horizon $r_+$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = -\left(\dfrac{r^2}{\ell_3^2} - M - \dfrac{\ell F}{r}\right)c^2dt^2 + \dfrac{dr^2}{\dfrac{r^2}{\ell_3^2} - M - \dfrac{\ell F}{r}} + r^2d\phi^2
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{\left(2r^3 + F\,\ell\,\ell_3^2\right)\left(r^3 - M\,\ell_3^2\,r - F\,\ell\,\ell_3^2\right)}{2\ell_3^4\,r^3}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{2r^3 + F\,\ell\,\ell_3^2}{2r\left(r^3 - M\,\ell_3^2\,r - F\,\ell\,\ell_3^2\right)}\dot{r}^2 + \dfrac{F\,\ell\,\ell_3^2 + M\,\ell_3^2\,r - r^3}{\ell_3^2}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(v, r, \phi)$, where the advanced time $v = ct + r_*$ is a length and the tortoise coordinate obeys $dr_*/dr = (r^2/\ell_3^2 - M - \ell F/r)^{-1}$ with $r_*(0) = 0$, and $r_+$ is the root of that denominator. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.

coordinates.name: C-Metric Brane

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius of the brane, a length; far from the hole the curvature is that of anti-de Sitter space with $\Lambda = -1/\ell_3^2$
Sign of the constant term, $\kappa = -1$ for the quantum BTZ black hole of positive mass and $\kappa = +1$ for a conical singularity dressed with a horizon, of negative mass

Mass parameter of the black hole in the bulk, dimensionless and not negative; the smallest positive root $x_1$ of $1 - \kappa x^2 - \mu x^3$ is the axis of the bulk, and $\mu = (1 - \kappa x_1^2)/x_1^3$ in the chart with no rotation

Strength of the backreaction of the quantum fields, a length, $\ell \simeq 2c_{\rm CFT}\hbar\mathcal{G}_3/c^3$ for small $\ell/\ell_3$ and a conformal field theory of central charge $c_{\rm CFT}$; at $\ell = 0$ the hole is the classical one of Bañados, Teitelboim, and Zanelli

coordinates.convention: We use the coordinates $(t, r, \phi)$ of the anti-de Sitter C-metric on the brane $x = 0$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, $\phi$ of period $2\pi\Delta$ with $\Delta = 2x_1/(3 - \kappa x_1^2)$, and $H = r^2/\ell_3^2 + \kappa - \mu\ell/r$, whose positive root is the horizon $r_+$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Rotating

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius of the brane, a length; far from the hole the curvature is that of anti-de Sitter space with $\Lambda = -1/\ell_3^2$
Sign of the constant term, $\kappa = -1$ for the quantum BTZ black hole of positive mass and $\kappa = +1$ for a conical singularity dressed with a horizon, of negative mass

Mass parameter of the black hole in the bulk, dimensionless and not negative; the smallest positive root $x_1$ of $1 - \kappa x^2 - \mu x^3$ is the axis of the bulk, and $\mu = (1 - \kappa x_1^2)/x_1^3$ in the chart with no rotation

Strength of the backreaction of the quantum fields, a length, $\ell \simeq 2c_{\rm CFT}\hbar\mathcal{G}_3/c^3$ for small $\ell/\ell_3$ and a conformal field theory of central charge $c_{\rm CFT}$; at $\ell = 0$ the hole is the classical one of Bañados, Teitelboim, and Zanelli
Rotation, a length, taken not negative; the hole with $a = 0$ does not rotate

coordinates.convention: We use the coordinates $(t, r, \phi)$ of the rotating anti-de Sitter C-metric on the brane $x = 0$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, and $H = r^2/\ell_3^2 + \kappa - \mu\ell/r + a^2/r^2$, whose two positive roots are the horizons $r_\pm$. Points are identified along $\phi \to \phi + 2\pi\Delta$ at fixed $ct + \tilde{a}\ell_3\phi$, with $\tilde{a} = ax_1^2/\ell_3$ and $\Delta = 2x_1/(3 - \kappa x_1^2 - \tilde{a}^2)$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
